{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZWIJMw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhC9dXM", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 25, "title": "Latch VDP1 erase data and windows at framebuffer changes", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

VDP1 does not retain a separate active copy of EWDR, EWLR and EWRR. At revision `d5a9861cd0c2243686dc31f1f43d41d5a91cb3af`, `Vdp1::write16` immediately replaces `self.erase`; `erase_area` reads those written values, and `start_blank_erase` calls it at VBlank. Consequently, preparing the next frame's erase color or rectangle can change the current frame's VBlank erase before a framebuffer change captures those settings.

This affects ordinary framebuffer management: software can clear the wrong rectangle or use the next frame's background color prematurely. Existing per-operation `EraseArea` retention protects an erase after it starts, but does not implement the preceding register-latch boundary.

## Expected outcome

Separate written erase settings from the settings captured at the documented framebuffer-change boundary. Both display-period erase and VBlank erase must consume the appropriate captured settings, and an accepted erase must retain its own configuration through completion or cancellation.

The primary contract is the VDP1 User's Manual ST-013-R3, [Chapter 4 register update timing](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp1/hon/p04_10.htm): erase data and coordinates take effect at framebuffer switching. [§4.2](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp1/hon/p04_12.htm) defines automatic/manual erase and change sequences; [§4.4](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp1/hon/p04_14.htm) defines rectangle units, pixel packing and erase budgets.

Preserve the distinction between written settings and internal state. In particular, [§4.9](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp1/hon/p04_19.htm) specifies that MODR reports register settings, which may differ from internally captured values. Its immediate readback is not a defect.

## Context and reproduction

Relevant implementation:

- `src/vdp1.rs:289–315`: register writes update the only erase-register array.
- `src/vdp1.rs:336–359`: framebuffer change captures EOS/DIE/DIL, but has no equivalent capture for erase registers.
- `src/vdp1.rs:362–377,399–418`: erase setup reads the latest written color and coordinates.
- `src/vdp1/progress_tests.rs:94–150`: existing vectors cover word deadlines and raster budgets, but do not establish a distinct previously captured configuration before replacing the written settings.

Create a focused reproduction that explicitly initializes configuration A and captures it through a framebuffer change, then writes a different configuration B before the following VBlank without another change. Current code constructs that VBlank erase from B; the required result uses the captured A. Following a subsequent framebuffer change, B must become effective. Use different colors and partially overlapping rectangles so color, extent and buffer identity are independently observable. Do not base expectations on undefined power-on register values.

Scope is the erase-parameter capture lifecycle and its integration with existing automatic/manual framebuffer control. Preserve immediate plot triggering, deferred drawing controls, MODR, scanline erase, retained erase jobs, VBlank termination and interrupt behavior. VBE sampling-phase corrections, half-line timing, new display modes and rasterizer changes remain separate work.

The #23 validation record reports 791 passing native tests and complete browser checks. The supplied current-main CI observation is still in progress; it establishes neither failure nor success. This planning pass used read-only source/specification inspection and did not rerun complete suites. A fresh open-Issue search returned no duplicates.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Add independent native vectors with explicitly initialized A/B/C colors and rectangles. Demonstrate written-versus-captured settings before and after framebuffer changes, including multiple writes before capture and held manual fields without a change. Derive literal expected pixels and register observations from the cited manual rules, without calling production erase-address helpers to generate expectations.
- [ ] Correct erase-setting capture and consumption for automatic changes, manual erase/change sequences and VBlank erase. Verify that pending writes cannot replace the captured configuration prematurely and that writes during an accepted erase cannot alter its retained color, bounds or destination buffer.
- [ ] Cover supported 16-bit and 8-bit framebuffer formats, including distinct even/odd erase bytes, rectangle edges and untouched canaries. Retain existing scanline-following erase, partial-budget and VBlank-OUT cancellation assertions. Correct historical fixture setup only with documented specification-derived reasoning; do not delete or weaken substantive assertions.
- [ ] Exercise real register transactions through both SH-2 adapters immediately before, at and after the relevant capture boundary. Assert physical write-completion ordering, identical results with advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000, and debugger-inspection invariance. Document equal-edge ordering as an emulator convention where the manual does not specify a physical phase.
- [ ] Verify reset cancellation of pending settings and unfinished erase work: no stale configuration or late erase write may affect a newly initialized run. Preserve existing framebuffer-change, EOS/DIE/DIL, PTMR, ENDR, EDSR/COPR/LOPR and SCU interrupt/DMA-trigger regressions. MODR must continue reporting written settings rather than being changed to report active latches.
- [ ] Add an original MIT-licensed SH-2 guest, reproducible source/builder and artifact hashes. The guest must program and synchronize the A/B capture sequence through real MMIO, compute its own result records and expose observable framebuffer differences. Run identical bytes in native Machine execution and production browser Wasm, with literal framebuffer and actual Canvas assertions, changed colors/coordinates, an omitted-write control and repeated cold boots. Host code may load fixtures and inspect results, but must not perform the guest's register sequence or draw its output.
- [ ] Demonstrate that the substantive new capture regression fails against the inherited implementation and passes with the correction. Record actual commands/results and distinguish this negative control from passing tests; do not generate golden output by recording the corrected emulator.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo clippy --locked --target wasm32-unknown-unknown -- -D warnings`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, existing fixture/media reproduction checks plus the new builder's `--check`, and complete `npm run test:browser` under `/saturn-rust/`, without required skips. Preserve Star Collector completion/restart, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab, audio, both controllers, backup RAM and browser privacy checks.
- [ ] Update the conformance matrix, architecture description where affected, and validation record with exact specification/implementation/test links and remaining deviations. Report this as a partial #17 increment. Other CPU/peripheral, multiprocessor/bus/reset, SCU/DSP, video/audio, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive acceptance requirements remain outstanding. Passing this task does not demonstrate broad commercial-game compatibility.

## Optional validation

None required. No personal firmware, commercial game files, physical console, human approval, live Pages inspection or tracker-closure investigation is needed.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
